title: Alpha Hands the Woman the Gun. YRF's First Female-Led Spy Film Names Her Sita and Lets Her Rewrite the Myth.
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari finally unite against Bobby Deol, the trailer ends on a pair of unmistakable green eyes, and the diaspora gets it the same weekend as Mumbai — July 3.
body:
The trailer opens not with a gunshot but with a name. **Bobby Deol**, all menace and stubble, leans over a kidnapped toddler and christens her Sita — after the mother he has just erased. It is a brutal, beautiful piece of mythmaking, and it tells you everything about what Yash Raj Films is attempting with **Alpha**: take the oldest story India knows, the princess abducted by a demon, and hand the woman a gun instead of a wait-to-be-rescued ending. By morning, the trailer was everywhere, and the verdict was loud — the YRF Spy Universe has finally let a woman run the show, and she is not asking permission.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

For two years, the Spy Universe has been a boys' club with a billion-rupee swagger — Salman's Tiger, Shah Rukh's Pathaan, Hrithik's Kabir, all glistening biceps and slow-motion entries. **Alpha**, out in theatres worldwide on **July 3**, is the franchise's seventh chapter and its first to put two women at the centre of the carnage. **Alia Bhatt** plays Sita, an assassin raised inside a shadow organisation called Alpha, trained by her adoptive father Fateh (Deol) until she discovers he has been pointing her at her own country. **Sharvari** is the other blade — and after fans dragged YRF for hiding her entirely in the teaser, the trailer finally gives her a colour-saturated, scene-stealing entrance, complete with a fight against Alia before the two inevitably join forces.

> "Working with Alia Bhatt is a masterclass for me." — Sharvari

That line has been doing the rounds, and on screen the dynamic reads exactly that way: Alia, the seasoned headliner, all coiled stillness, against Sharvari's livewire kineticism. The chemistry between them — combative, then conspiratorial — is the trailer's real engine, more electric than any of the gunfire. And there is plenty of gunfire. Director **Shiv Rawail**, making his feature debut after the acclaimed series *The Railway Men*, stages chase sequences across monasteries and snowbound Kashmir valleys, the action choreographed by Craig Macrae and Sunil Rodrigues with a cold, kinetic precision that owes more to Bourne than to the chest-thumping Spy Universe house style.

Then comes the cliffhanger that broke the internet. The final shot lands inside a monastery, where a figure in white sits waiting to help the two women on their mission. The camera holds. Green eyes. **Hrithik Roshan's** Kabir Dhaliwal, back from the *War* franchise, his cameo now officially confirmed. It is a fan-service flourish executed with just enough restraint to feel earned rather than desperate, and the diaspora WhatsApp groups lit up within minutes.



The industry has been unusually generous with its applause. **Sonam Kapoor** called it "a refreshing change… cool to see girls at the centre of an action entertainer." **Janhvi Kapoor** reposted the trailer to her Stories, gushing about "two badass women" while throwing a shoutout to her chachu **Anil Kapoor**, who turns up here as Colonel Vikrant Kaul, the steely chief of R&AW. The casting alone — Alia, Sharvari, Anil, Bobby, Hrithik, with Dia Mirza in the mix — is the kind of ensemble that makes a film feel like an event before a single ticket is sold.

What makes Alpha genuinely interesting, though, is what it refuses to be. YRF has confirmed there is no India-Pakistan spy-friendship angle here, none of the joint-mission sentimentality the franchise has leaned on before. This is a colder, more internal story — a woman discovering she has been weaponised against her own people and deciding to turn the blade around. Sita rewriting Sita. The mythological echo is not subtle, and it is not meant to be.

For the diaspora, the timing is a gift. **Alpha** releases in theatres worldwide on July 3, which means NRIs in the US, UK and Canada get it the same weekend as audiences in Mumbai — no agonising wait, no spoiler-dodging on Twitter. Expect wide releases across AMC and Cineworld screens, with the usual YRF muscle behind the overseas push. The film will eventually stream, almost certainly on Prime Video given YRF's recent output, but this is one built for the big screen and the booming surround sound of an action set-piece.

There is, naturally, a rival in the ring. Huma Qureshi's *Baby Do Die Do*, another desi female-assassin film, lands the very same day — a clash that has its own delicious subtext about how many women-led action films the market can hold. The honest answer, on the evidence of this trailer, is that there is room for both. But only one of them has green eyes waiting in a monastery. Alia Bhatt has never looked more dangerous, and the Spy Universe has never looked more alive.
